newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise to new highs, seen correcting.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise to new highs, seen correcting.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds rose to new highs on Wednesday as the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond advanced, dealers said.
But they expected MinFin bonds to ease in the next few days as investors, nervous before a slew of U.S. economic data, take profits.
On Thursday, the U.S. will issue the jobless claims index and on Friday, the monthly non-farm payroll figure is due.

"We have risen fantastically. We are at a new historical high," said Raiffeisen Bank trader Alexander Chernyatin. "This is because of the rise of the (U.S.) long bond, plus there was no bad news from Russia."
A Bank Imperial dealer said MinFins became more dependant on U.S. Treasuries as the spread betweeen the papers narrowed in the past several months.
Chernyatin said the spread on the benchmark tranche 3 had halved to 270 basis points at Tuesday's close from 540 bp at the end of 1996.
He forecast the market would slip in the next few days.
"The market will sink in profit-taking," he said. "The figures are too important and those who have a chance to take profits will do so to be on the safe side."

The Bank Imperial dealer said the market was watching the International Monetary Fund mission's activities. The IMF mission is currently in Moscow to discuss disbursing the next tranche of the fund's $10 billion loan to Russia.
"A negative decision will have a more serious impact than a positive one," he said. "If they say they will extend the next tranche, there will be no strong rise, as everyone expects it."
